resolved_conflicts.explanation: The association gives a 50-foot pole L-4 tower for 1935. A 1959 Coast and Geodetic Survey description gives an overall height of 60 feet (18.3 m), which is the figure kept in facts. The sources do not explain the gap.
The association says destroyed in 1976; the Montana listing marks the NGS record as removed, with no date. Both say the tower is gone, so the story reports both.

sources.title: Trails of the Past: Historical Overview of the Flathead National Forest

notes_for_editor: Two sources give different heights for the structure (50 ft vs 60 ft overall); the brief's 18.3 m matches the 1959 NGS figure, so it is kept and the gap is recorded. Map and place-listing sites (anyplaceamerica, pastmaps 2011 topo, opengovca) still show 'Ashley Mountain Lookout Tower' as a label; these are not evidence of a standing structure and are not used in the story. The FFLA page has a 'Photo courtesy the Fire Lookout Museum' credit with no image URL in the cache, so no photo was added. Search budget used: 2 searches.
